The Pan Niger Delta Forum has called on the Inspector-General of Police and the Department of State Services to investigate the reported killings and attacks on supporters of the National Democratic Congress during a political rally in Delta State. The forum urged security agencies to identify and prosecute those who masterminded, sponsored, or participated in the violence. In a statement issued in Abuja on Thursday, PANDEF National Chairman, Ambassador Godknows Igali, condemned the violence at a recent political rally organised by the NDC in parts of Ughelli, Delta State. Igali said media reports indicated that some persons lost their lives, while several others sustained varying degrees of injuries. Consequently, the former ambassador to Norway, Sweden and Denmark urged the police, DSS and other relevant security agencies to conduct a comprehensive, impartial and thorough investigation into the circumstances surrounding the incident. Delta prosecuting over 15 human trafficking cases — Official Nwoko’s supporter injured during APC primary dies Kwara violence: AbdulRazaq accuses Saraki of arming youths The PANDEF chairman recalled that the organisation had warned only last week against political violence, intimidation, and intolerance of opposition parties in the South-South region. He said the region had historically demonstrated commendable traditions of political sportsmanship, tolerance and civility in the conduct of elections. Igali expressed concern that the reported attack in Ughelli occurred barely days after the forum appealed to communities in the region to remain vigilant against political violence. “There is absolutely no place in our democratic practice for such levels of violence, brutality and desperation for political power,” he said. The forum warned that any breakdown of law and order in the oil-producing region could have serious implications for Nigeria’s economic and national security, given its strategic importance to the country’s oil and gas revenues. It also called on the Federal Government, relevant federal agencies and the Delta State Government to provide support to families of those reportedly killed and ensure that injured victims received adequate medical attention. PANDEF stressed that political competition must be guided by tolerance, respect for opposing views and peaceful participation.
